objective: Produce a technical decision document that captures system design, implementation constraints, and engineering trade-offs for this feature — ready to guide implementation.

role.instruction: You are acting as a technical decision maker. Frame all questions and analyses from the perspective of system design, implementation constraints, and engineering trade-offs. Use technical vocabulary (architecture, dependencies, interfaces, rollback) rather than product vocabulary.

domain.name: technical
domain.instruction: Frame all gate dialogue and decision-doc content from the perspective of system design and engineering trade-offs for implementing this feature. Technical identifiers, architecture terms, and implementation references are appropriate in this domain.

acceptance_criteria.goal: Implementation completion can be determined objectively against the decision.
acceptance_criteria.question: What observable and verifiable technical outcomes would demonstrate that this decision has been implemented successfully?
acceptance_criteria.completion: Complete when 3–6 outcome-level criteria cover the intended behavior and critical constraints, each verifiable through observable system behavior or evidence—not subjective judgment, implementation steps, individual test names, or assertions.

impact_surface.goal: All technical change surfaces required to implement and verify the decision are made explicit.
impact_surface.question: Which responsibility surfaces and implementation-stack layers does this decision affect, and how do they map to each other?
impact_surface.completion: Complete when all affected systems, modules, interfaces, and external parties are identified and mapped to the relevant implementation areas—such as storage, services, UI, MCP, and tests; granularity stops at layer, module, directory, or interface boundaries—not individual files or test cases.

external_dependencies.goal: Dependencies outside the feature’s change set have explicit and verifiable commitments.
external_dependencies.question: Which external capabilities or components does the decision rely on, who owns them, and what must each dependency provide, change, or preserve?
external_dependencies.completion: Complete when every genuine external dependency specifies its owner, required behavior or state—including changes such as upgrades—contract, authoritative source, and confirmation mechanism; unresolved facts are recorded as Assumptions.

implementation_sketch.goal: The decision has a coherent and implementable technical shape, with its constraints and reversibility understood.
implementation_sketch.question: What key technical changes realize this decision, how do they work together, what non-obvious constraints or complexity shape them, and how can they be reversed?
implementation_sketch.completion: Complete when the key changes and their interactions are described, critical constraints or complexity and reversibility are explicit, and unresolved constraints are recorded as Assumptions; remain at change-shape level—not individual files, tasks, or patches.

gap_check.goal: No mismatch between the expected implementation output and the acceptance criteria remains hidden.
gap_check.question: Does the expected implementation output satisfy every acceptance criterion, and where does it fall short?
gap_check.completion: Complete when all acceptance criteria have been checked against the expected implementation output and a one-line verdict records either full coverage or any shortfall—without a separate breakdown.
